subject: Nectar Retail: post-black-friday performance recovery & next steps
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@nectar-retail.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nectar-retail.com>
Date: 2027-11-24T08:12:00Z
Subject: Nectar Retail: Latency and 500s during BFCM window

Kimberly / Redwood team,

We saw a substantial spike in end-to-end latency and ~2.1% 5xx rate across our inference-heavy checkout flows from 02:00–06:00 PST on 2027-11-24 (Black Friday peak). Customer-facing errors impacted roughly 8% of sessions for certain SKUs. Our ops pulled logs and attached a tarball (spike_logs.tar.gz) showing request traces and sampling of error stacks.

We need:
- Immediate confirmation of root cause and mitigation already applied.
- An executive summary of customer impact and estimated contract credit.
- A timeline for the permanent fix and validation plan.

This was material for our weekend revenue and we need an expedited readout. Please escalate.

Thanks,
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Platform Reliability
Nectar Retail

Attachment: spike_logs.tar.gz

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@nectar-retail.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nectar-retail.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-24T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Nectar Retail: Latency and 500s during BFCM window

Hi Sarah — thank you for the heads up and the logs. I’m escalating this to our on-call infra and inference teams now (cc’d). Initial mitigation we’ve applied:
- temporarily increased dedicated concurrency for Nectar’s pool and enabled a fallback to a lower-context variant to reduce per-request memory pressure
- enabled stricter rate shaping for non-critical background routes to prioritize checkout traffic

We propose a 30-minute Zoom to walk through what we see and align on next steps; are you available at 11:30 PST?

I’ll follow up with a preliminary technical summary and an estimated account impact/crystalized credit proposal after we validate the initial mitigations.

Kimberly Park
Senior AM, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@nectar-retail.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-25T09:00:00Z
Subject: RE: Nectar Retail: Latency and 500s during BFCM window — preliminary findings and proposed fixes

Sarah / team — following the logs and internal traces, here’s our preliminary findings (short version):

What happened (prelim):
- Autoscaler gating for sequence-length distribution did not trigger fast enough under the sudden burst of long-context requests. This caused an accumulation of large KV cache evictions and increased token-generation latency per request.
- Under pressure, the serving runtime’s continuous batching heuristics pushed some requests onto a path with higher memory amplification which led to elevated OOM/soft-failure fallbacks manifesting as 500s.

Immediate actions taken:
- Pinned Nectar pool to a conservative kernel profile for the duration of the recovery window (completed 11/24 11:15 PST).
- Applied a hotfix to lower the batch assembly timeout for long-context routes; this reduced the median tail by ~230ms in our test harness.
- Restored a KV-cache guard that prevents aggressive eviction when memory pressure crosses the 73% threshold.

Attachments: rca_draft.pdf (contains timeline + log excerpts), spike_logs.tar.gz (from your upload)

Planned permanent changes (timeline):
- Week 1: deploy autoscaler gating improvements and add sequence-length-aware admission control (canary to 10% of Nectar traffic)
- Week 2–3: kernel-selection tuning + extended load tests to validate under synthetic peak workloads
- Week 4: full rollout and post-deployment monitoring for two weekend peaks

We’ll also prepare an exec-level one-pager for you with estimated customer impact and a credit proposal. Laura, can you help coordinate the commercial ask?

-Neha
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@nectar-retail.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nectar-retail.com>
Date: 2027-11-26T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Nectar Retail: Latency and 500s during BFCM window — preliminary findings and proposed fixes

Thanks Neha — that context helps. A few asks from our side:

1) Exec summary with revenue / session impact and proposed credit estimate (we log $1.4M incremental revenue during the affected window; want a clear method for credit calculation).
2) Clear SLA remediation commitments and a soft timeline that we can send internally to our CFO.
3) Weekly checkpoint for the first two weeks after the permanent rollout.

Please include the contract excerpt (I’ve attached the relevant page). We’ll expect an official credit proposal and the fix timeline by COB Monday, 2027-11-29.

Appreciate the fast response.

Regards,
Sarah

Attachment: contract_sla_excerpt.pdf

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@nectar-retail.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nectar-retail.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-27T11:05:00Z
Subject: Nectar Retail — Executive impact summary, remediation commitments, and proposed account credit

Sarah / Tom — thank you for the clear asks. Below is an executive-summary style readout and our proposed next steps. We will also upload a formal credit proposal doc to HubSpot by COB Monday (2027-11-29).

Executive impact (concise):
- Incident window: 2027-11-24 02:00–06:00 PST.
- Customer-facing session impact: ~8% of checkout sessions affected; sampling suggests ~2.1% surfaced 5xx errors.
- Estimated incremental revenue potentially lost during window: $1.4M (per Nectar’s report). Our conservative estimation of directly attributable loss: $320k–$480k after filtering for retries and funnel abandonment patterns.

Mitigation & permanent remediation timeline:
- Completed (immediate): capacity pinning, KV-cache guard, smaller batch timeout (11/24).
- Short-term (canary 10%): autoscaler gating + admission control (target: 2027-11-30).
- Medium-term (full rollout + load tests): kernel-selection tuning and extended validation (target window: 2027-12-07 to 2027-12-14).
- Monitoring: two-week elevated telemetry with daily checkpoint calls and a Nagios-style incident dashboard for Nectar (shared link below).

Commercial proposal:
- We propose a one-time account credit equivalent to 40% of the conservative direct-impact estimate (midpoint ~$400k ⇒ proposed credit $160k). This is subject to final reconciliation of logs and funnel attribution and is detailed in the formal proposal we’ll upload. Laura will work with your procurement to finalize wording.

Next steps / checkpoints:
- 2027-11-29 COB: formal credit proposal posted to HubSpot (kimberly to post).
- 2027-11-30 10:00 PST: canary deployment kicks off (neha will run).
- Weekly checkpoints: Tuesdays 09:00 PST for 2 weeks after full rollout; invite will be sent.

Links / artifacts:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/98765
- Jira ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123
- Draft RCA: attached (rca_draft.pdf)

If this looks acceptable we’ll proceed to the formal credit doc and schedule the canary. Thank you for working through this with us — we know this was impactful for your holiday weekend.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior AM, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
